question: Can a CPU-only Slurm allocation on an H200-host node supply receiver measurement evidence for a later real H200 GPU Slurm job?
answer: Yes in principle: no job-ID or GPU-allocation/visibility equality makes that reuse intrinsically impossible. Admissibility remains conditional on exact native deployment/software/source/reference equality, compatible process/cgroup scopes, authentic measurement provenance and all original resource/admission guards.
scope: Read-only exact source310 and accepted278-r2 receiver path; no allocation, measurement, native import, test, implementation, scheduler or model action.

required_equal_to_later_actual_consumer.rule: Exactly slurm for both noninjected CPU measurement and GPU consumer. The only alternative class in this projector is injected; there is no CPU-versus-GPU class split.

Exact platform.machine() and first available /proc/cpuinfo model-name/Processor/cpu-model string. Same H200 label alone is insufficient. Node hostname, CPU stepping and CPU topology are not additional members here.

Exact equality to the independently observed later GPU allocation projection at loader entry. CPU and memory must be positive integers, cluster a nonempty string. Matching at least the GPU contract is insufficient for this entry equality, even though completed intake also has a separate minimum-capacity check.

Exact dictionary equality per actual target/preparation object root. Path is resolve(strict=True); mount_point is the deepest containing mount from /proc/self/mountinfo; filesystem and mount_source come from that mount; device is stat().st_dev. Same bytes or same underlying filesystem alone is insufficient. A different private bind mount point can fail even on the same host and same data.

Exact current _prepared_environment(False) dictionary. Platform is platform.system(), deployment_family is slurm-receiver and storage_family is per-path-mount-evidence. This exact tuple does not include GPU count, CUDA visibility, CUDA runtime/device properties, hostname or Slurm job ID. Broader software authenticity remains an existing root provenance obligation.

required_equal_to_later_actual_consumer.field: record.references, source_identity, reader_sha256, freeze_sha256, recipe and scope
required_equal_to_later_actual_consumer.rule: Exact target/preparation byte references and paths, commit/code/design/protocol identity, current runtime/workload whole-file hashes and original accounting recipe/scope. The measurement run must independently agree with all those fields and before/after code hashes. The measurement provenance object must remain complete, reachable and byte-identical.

required_equal_to_later_actual_consumer.field: process observation scope and cgroup applicability/scope
required_equal_to_later_actual_consumer.rule: Each measured process scope must equal the later native process_peak_scope: process lifetime high-water RSS on Linux. Each measured cgroup applicable boolean must equal whether the later native cgroup_scope is non-null; scope must equal that native string, or not applicable when unavailable. CPU/GPU jobs with different native cgroup-v2 availability are incomparable, even on one host. Raw wrapper v1/ancestry observations cannot be relabelled as native v2 applicability.

required_provenance_not_equal_to_later_j.rule: Required nonempty string and must truthfully identify the CPU measurement allocation. Not compared to later GPU job_id. Its allocation cluster/cpus/memory projection must equal deployment.allocation_family.

Run PID is a positive integer; both measurement phases must use that same PID. Not compared to later consumer PID. Actual distinct new-executable launcher evidence is still required for the cold phase.

Required nonempty real path when applicable, but NOT required equal to the later job's literal cgroup path. The reconciliation function explicitly compares classes/scopes rather than job-specific path literals. Cold/warm internal equality also compares applicability/scope, not path literals.

required_provenance_not_equal_to_later_j.field: run_id, normal completion, exit code, phase timings and raw process/cgroup observations
required_provenance_not_equal_to_later_j.rule: Truthful source-bound internal provenance: run_id matches measurement, normal_completion true, exit_code zero, cold/warm phase dictionaries identical between run and measurement, correct fresh-process/same-process-repeat labels, nonnegative finite wall/user/system, valid RSS/peak/events. These are observations/requirements, not a demand to equal later consumer timings or numerical measurements.

not_members_of_receiver_deployment_equal: Slurm job_id, step_id, account, partition, QoS, requested walltime, NodeList or hostname
GPU TRES/count/type/physical presence, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and other SLURM GPU environment variables
process PID or literal cgroup path
directory inode or mount ID; storage does include st_dev, resolved path and deepest mount metadata
CUDA build/device properties or Transformers version as independent environment keys (torch_version and original source/provenance checks still apply)
important_boundaries: H200-host placement is a scheduling strategy to find the same CPU family/storage/software; the measurement context does not require a GPU allocation or physical H200 label. A generic RM placement is not automatically valid, though no extra hardware-label field exists beyond the stated equality tuple.

Different clusters, CPU/RAM allocations, CPU model strings, Python/library versions, resolved object roots, mount layouts or storage st_dev values fail exact equality. Same host or same filesystem name does not waive any field.

The production loader supplies independently observed actual GPU allocation context, compares it with original admission receiver_deployment, validates resources before reading, and rechecks context after reading. The data-only default validator fallback is not permission to manufacture matching allocation evidence.

Applicable native cgroup observations require true current/peak/events and exact whole-current-cgroup lifetime scope. Unavailable requires reason cgroup-v2-observations-unavailable and scope not applicable. Process/cgroup paths and lifetime peaks retain true provenance; no sample establishes an upper bound.

Accepted receiver adapter calls only untouched lower reader and one final witness per trial, retains the exact result, releases it before same-process warm repeat, and requires real new-executable provenance. It neither calls the authority loader nor needs a GPU to mint a handle, because no handle is minted.

Same deployment tuple is necessary but not sufficient: actual conservative resource bounds/capacity, authentic retained production handle accounting, original final live/scope/deadline barrier, source adoption/native/numerical and original GPU allocation/admission/ledger/lease guards remain unchanged. A later GPU job still needs its actual H200 authority; CPU measurement grants none.

scheduler_context_root_reported.reason: Jobs requesting no GPU resources must only be submitted to CPU partitions
scheduler_context_root_reported.scope: root-reported previews, not a scheduler query by this worker; ordinary direct CPU-only placement on those partitions unavailable

bounded_existing_cpu_provenance.scope: historical actual CPU receipt only, not current node interrogation or receiver applicability; architecture/current consumer CPU family not established

inspected: named historical A3 N5 evidence allocation/environment/run manifest
bounded_H200_cpu_model_search.limitation: No broad tree scan or live node/scheduler/SSH/native action; do not infer H200 CPU model from GPU type or CPU partition hostname

no_GPU_escape.rule: Do not spend a GPU solely to escape CPU-only placement rejection; establish actual CPU-family/context match through root-owned existing provenance/scheduler evidence or report unresolved placement
